headline: AI adoption in go-to-market hiring is slower than sentiment suggests, with only 17% of roles requiring AI skills over the past 90 days
reasoning: Ricky Pearl from Pointer Strategy found that only 17% of go-to-market job advertisements in the past 90 days mentioned AI as a required skill, suggesting a significant gap between perceived AI impact and actual hiring behaviour. The requirement rises to over 30% for more senior roles, indicating firms are concentrating AI deployment decisions at higher levels. Companies appear to be extending the productivity of existing headcount rather than hiring new AI-skilled staff, reflecting hesitation about how to effectively deploy the technology. There is also a distinction between firms looking to 'buy' AI skills externally versus developing them internally.
quote: That 17% is the average across all of the go to market rolls. And this specifically is looking at go to market roles. You know everything that touches revenue really for for most businesses other than retail. And that 17% is the average. So as you get more senior, the requirement does go all the way up to over 30%. Um, and I think what we're finding is there is still a lot of hesitation around how to use AI. How is it going to be effective. And so the requirements are still sitting with more senior employees that maybe would get to have a decision as to how AI might be deployed, rather than making it a requirement on junior employees.

headline: A 37% quarterly drop in go-to-market job postings signals a meaningful slowdown in economic growth intentions, though early signs of recovery have emerged
reasoning: Pearl argues that go-to-market roles are a leading indicator of economic health because companies will delay back-office hiring but rarely cut roles that directly generate revenue. A 37% decline in total go-to-market roles coming to market over the most recent quarter is therefore a significant warning signal about economic growth appetite. However, Pearl notes that the most recent two weeks have seen a slight uptick in postings, providing a tentative early sign of stabilisation. AI-driven productivity gains among existing staff are reducing the urgency to hire, compounding the headline decline.
quote: So we saw over the quarter for this last quarter, a 37% decrease in total rolls coming on the market, which was pretty significant.
